description: Cut your AI coding agent's token bill on three axes: terse prose, YAGNI-first code, and tool-output compression. Claude Code, Pi, Cursor, Codex, Gemini + 4 more. Zero deps, published benchmarks including the runs it loses.

latest_release.name: v3.14.2
latest_release.body:
# Changelog

All notable changes to Chisle are documented here.
Format loosely follows [Keep a Changelog](https://keepachangelog.com/).

## [Unreleased]

## [3.14.2] - 2026-11-19

Patch: the star prompt reports star and follow separately, and the site shows each agent's logo.

### Docs
- Site: the "Thirteen agents, one install" grid shows each agent's logo (LobeHub Icons, MIT, `site/public/logos/LICENSE`) in the page's text color, instead of two-letter tiles.

### Fixed
- Star prompt: a `y` reported "Couldn't use gh" even when the star went through. Star and follow are now separate calls with separate messages: gh's default login can star but lacks the `user:follow` scope, so a failed follow prints the scope hint and the link, and the repo owner is never asked to follow themselves.

## [3.14.1] - 2026-11-19

Patch: the star prompt defaults to "later", and the README, site and docs move to the full 3.14 benchmark run.

### Changed
- The installer's star prompt gains "later", now the default: `[y]es / [n]o / [L]ater`. Enter, `l` or an answer it can't read saves nothing and asks again at the next install or update; only an explicit `y` or `n` is saved.

### Docs
- Full benchmark suite re-run for 3.14 beside 3.13, caveman and ponytail (`docs/benchmarks.md`), raw cells committed, plus `ANSWERS.md` beside each side-by-side run with every prompt and every arm's verbatim answer (`benchmarks/answers.js`). Billed output on Haiku 4.5: Chisle 69%, caveman 69%, ponytail 80%; Chisle's answers are shortest (51%). Accuracy 156/156 for bare and Chisle. Agentic, 3.14 vs 3.13: context 88%, tool output read 80%.
- README, translations and site move to these numbers. The tagline now says "Shorter answers than caveman and ponytail": billed tokens tie with caveman in this run. New README chart for the input axis: terminal output Claude reads over 37 commands, caveman and ponytail 100%, RTK 84%, Chisle 28%. The filter card shows a failing run filtered by the wrapper.

## [3.14.0] - 2026-11-19

Minor: failed test and build runs filtered on Claude Code, and more RTK-style command filters (git, ls, wc, grep, go, cargo). The design follows [RTK](https://github.com/rtk-ai/rtk); no RTK code is used (see NOTICE).

### Added
- **Failed test and build runs get filtered on Claude Code.** Claude Code hands a failed command's output to `PostToolUseFailure`, which cannot rewrite it. A new `PreToolUse` hook (`hooks/chisle-run.js`) now runs test, build and install commands through a Node wrapper that filters stdout and stderr like the compression hook and keeps the exit status. It wraps only the matching segments of a command (`cd app && npm test` → `cd app && <wrapper> npm test`) and skips what it cannot parse safely: subshells, `$(...)`, background jobs, heredocs, watch mode, `sudo`. Claude Code checks permission rules against the rewritten command, so the wrapper runs only in `bypassPermissions` mode and never for a program named by a deny or ask `Bash(...)` rule. `CHISLE_COMPRESS_WRAP=1` enables it in every mode and `=0` turns it off. Not on Windows.
- **More command filters, following RTK's output shapes.** Long `git status` becomes the short `XY path` form. Default `git log` and `git show` get one header line per commit (10-char hash, subject, day, author without email; a shared author is named once). `git diff`, `git show` and `git log -p` headers shrink to one path line. `--stat` loses its bars and padding. `git branch -a` folds each remote onto one line. `ls -l` gives an octal mode (ACL/xattr mark kept), size and name, keeps `.` for the directory's own mode and names the owner unless it is you, `wc` drops padding, and `grep -rn`/`rg` print each path once. `cargo test` drops its banners, empty suites, zero counts and the repeated failure list. `go test -v` drops passing tests whole, header and log lines, so no log line ends up beside a failure it did not come from.

- The installer asks once, at the end of an interactive install or update, whether to star t

English · Español · 한국어 · 简体中文 · 日本語

Shorter answers than caveman and ponytail. No accuracy lost.

```bash npx chisle ```

See both answers
The prompt: *"Implement an order state machine covering created, paid, shipped, delivered, cancelled and refunded, with the legal transitions enforced and invalid ones rejected."* Excerpts from the verbatim committed answers in [`raw-314-sidebyside/large-s2`](benchmarks/results/raw-314-sidebyside/large-s2/):
no ruleset: 126 lines, 1,571 answer tokensChisle: 58 lines, 567 answer tokens
```python class OrderStateMachine: VALID_TRANSITIONS: Dict[OrderState, Set[OrderState]] = { OrderState.CREATED: {OrderState.PAID, OrderState.CANCELLED}, … } def can_transition_to(self, next_state: OrderState) -> bool: """Check if transition from current state to next state is valid.""" def transition_to(self, next_state: OrderState) -> None: """Transition to the next state. Raises ValueError if transition is invalid.""" def get_current_state(self) -> str: def get_valid_next_states(self) -> Set[str]: ``` …all inside a file-write tool call it could not make (tools were off), plus a four-scenario demo, a feature list and a recap of the transitions. ```python class OrderStateMachine: VALID_TRANSITIONS = { OrderState.CREATED: {OrderState.PAID, OrderState.CANCELLED}, OrderState.PAID: {OrderState.SHIPPED, OrderState.CANCELLED, OrderState.REFUNDED}, … } def transition(self, new_state: OrderState) -> None: """Transition to new_state or raise ValueError if invalid.""" if new_state not in self.VALID_TRANSITIONS[self.state]: raise ValueError( f"Cannot transition from {self.state.value} to {new_state.value}" ) self.state = new_state ``` Then a short usage block and a one-line recap of the transitions.

Every raw transcript is committed, losses included. Method and data · why we publish the losses

Other ways to install
```bash # Claude Code plugin marketplace claude plugin marketplace add JayPokale/Chisle claude plugin install chisle@chisle # curl curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/JayPokale/Chisle/main/install.sh | bash ``` ```powershell # Windows irm https://raw.githubusercontent.com/JayPokale/Chisle/main/install.ps1 | iex ``` Per-agent setup, upgrading and config: [docs/usage.md](docs/usage.md).

⭐ Star the repo: it costs zero tokens. · Follow @JayPokale for more tools.

MIT · Contributing · Began as a merge of caveman and ponytail (notices) · Command filters follow RTK's design
